question: On standard tabular binary classification datasets, how well calibrated are the predicted probabilities of logistic regression, random forests and gradient-boosted trees without recalibration, and how much do Platt scaling and isotonic regression fitted on held-out data change calibration error and log-loss?
hypotheses: H1 (replication of a known result; Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana 2005): without recalibration, random forests have higher calibration error than logistic regression on most datasets.
H2a (contested in prior work): isotonic regression fitted on held-out data reduces the calibration error of random forests on most datasets.
H2b (open for modern log-loss gradient boosting): isotonic regression fitted on held-out data reduces the calibration error of scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier on most datasets.
contribution: A seed-resolved, per-model and per-dataset replication of known calibration results, with the base model held fixed across recalibration methods, and a clean test of whether isotonic recalibration helps random forests (contested) and modern log-loss gradient boosting (open in the work we found).

tasks.title: Prior work on calibration of tabular classifiers and post-hoc recalibration (Platt; Zadrozny-Elkan; Niculescu-Mizil-Caruana; calibration metrics)
